trajectory_summary: The call opens with mild customer curiosity about the speed of the callback, but the rep never converts that into a real qualifying conversation — no bill amount, no interest-reason probe, no address/homeowner check. Instead the rep leads with an unconditional savings guarantee before having any customer-specific data, and when the customer presses for real numbers three separate times, the rep has nothing to offer but restated promises. The call ends with the customer requesting a website link and a vague 'I'll call you back' — an unanchored exit with no appointment, no callback time, and no next step owned by the rep.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unspecified but nothing here supports 'booked' or 'tentative' — the call ends on 'Okay. I'll call you back. Bye.' with no day/time and no rep-owned follow-up, which is a no_appointment outcome, not a soft callback the rep secured.

primary_coaching_focus.quote: But you don't know what I'm paying now.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer explicitly names the exact gap in the rep's pitch — the rep doesn't know his bill — three separate times across the call, and the rep never once asks for the actual bill amount or utility usage. This single missed question is why the guarantee at 00:59 sounds hollow and why the call ends without any real qualifying data captured.

key_moments.quote: I'm not selling anything. I'm appointment setting.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep never framed the purpose of the call in the opening (no reference to the form, no legitimacy anchor) — so the customer's very next question is 'what are you selling', a sign the intro didn't do its job. The rep's clarification here is defensive, coming after the customer already sensed a pitch rather than being told upfront.

key_moments.quote: And if we can't save you money in the first year and remove that bill, we're not gonna offer anything at all.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is a blanket guarantee delivered before any bill amount, usage figure, or utility company was captured. It reads as an unconditional promise the rep has no data to back, and it directly sets up the customer's three-part demand for actual rates later in the call.

key_moments.quote: I'm I'm asking what those rates are that you would be paying. It'll always be cheaper than what you're paying now. It can never be higher. But you don't know what I'm paying now.

The rep does not pick this up; the transcript shows no subsequent question about the customer's actual bill.
